messages.subject: Strange behaviour in session control or environment control?
messages.subject_clean: Strange behaviour in session control or environment control?
messages.body_plain:
I use rapache for generation of questionnair reports.
Now as a test I had the following simple brew script:

<%
print(ls())
%>

I would expect that on each call a new session is started up, so that this always prints an empty list(character(0). I suppose the user is www-data, and this user does not have a ~/.RData file
If the script is called several times, however, sometimes (or often), a list of objects is displayed, probably from another session. You can try this at http://www.dpvragenlijst.nl/z/boe

Is this intended behaviour? I can not expect that. And is there a way to prevent this? This appears to be very dangerous.

Is this the same problem as in https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rapache/vAQot_kzEIM ?

Thanks

Frans

messages.subject_clean: Strange behaviour in session control or environment control?
messages.body_plain:
I know this might seem strange when you first learn this, but its a property of rApache applications. The web server creates many child processes which all serve many clients. If you want to maintain state per client then you'll need to build that layer yourself. A popular approach is to set a cookie in the client browser with a unique Id and store the client state keyed off the Id in a database. rApache is a foundational layer that web application frameworks sit on top of. Although none exist right now, I'm hopeful someone may come along and write one. messages.body_plain:
Hi masters of R I found out what happened. I would not call it error, but it is really "unexpected behaviour". The script is called with something like. "//www.dpvragenlijst.nl/z/boe?boem=ho " Then GET$boem has the value "ho" But when the script is called without a parameter, I wanted a default value. For that reason I have the statement "if (is.null(GET)) {GET<-list();GET$boem<-"default value"} This causes the problem: the environment may have a GET object from another session. And then GET does not have the expected value (the script is called without a parameter, but GET still has a value. So probably the lesson is to never create a GET object, just read it. What I still do not understand: what kind of object is GET? print(class(GET)) indicated GET is a list. But print(ls()) does not show it? messages.subject: How to create temp.dir() when deploying Rook apps with rapache?
messages.subject_clean: How to create temp.dir() when deploying Rook apps with rapache?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to deploy the Hmisc example from Rook through rapache.

config.R from Hmisc looks like this:
--------------------------------------------------
library(Hmisc)
dir.create(file.path(tempdir(),'plots'),showWarnings=FALSE)
app <- Builder$new(

    Static$new(
    urls = c('/css','/images','/javascript'),
    root = '.'
    ),
    Static$new(urls='/plots',root=tempdir()),
    Brewery$new(
    url='/brew',
    root='.',
    imagepath=file.path(tempdir(),'plots'),
    imageurl='../plots/'
    ),
    Redirect$new('/brew/useR2007.rhtml')
)
-------------------------------------------

In my apache config I used:
------------------------------------------
<Location /Hmisc>
SetHandler r-handler
REval "library(Hmisc)"
RFileEval /var/www/Hmisc/config.R:Rook::Server$call(app)
</Location>
----------------------------------------------

But I could not figure out where to place: dir.create(file.path(tempdir(),'plots'),showWarnings=FALSE)

Thanks for any hints/suggestions

Johannes

messages.subject: Check installed version of rApache
messages.subject_clean: Check installed version of rApache
messages.body_plain:
I am working on automating the installation of rApache (using Chef).  One thing I need to do is skip the compilation and installation if the version of rApache I want is already installed.  Is there a way to tell which version of rApache is installed?

The options I see are:
1) Check if mod_R.so exists.  This allows me to skip installation if rApache is already installed, but it does not support upgrading rApache if the installed version is old.
2) Add an r-info url and check that.  However, this requires r-info to be running, which we may not want in production.  It also requires httpd to be running which may not be the case while the server is being provisioned.
3) After installing rApache, write a metadata file with the version installed.

Is there a more standard way of checking the version of rApache?  I tried using `nm mod_R.so` and `objdump -x mod_R.so` but I did not see anything I could use.

Thanks

messages.subject: New rApache builds for Apache 2.4
messages.subject_clean: New rApache builds for Apache 2.4
messages.body_plain:
The rapache deb package (libapache2-mod-r-base) has been updated to work with the new Apache 2.4, which replaces Apache 2.2 in Debian 8 and Ubuntu 13.10. With the upgrade to Apache2.4, The Debian team has refactored and renamed the Apache2 related packages, and therefore the rapache control file had to be modified to accommodate these changes:

- Package apache2-mpm-prefork is now a virtual package provided by apache2-dev
- Package apache2.2-common has been replaced by apache2-bin
- Package libapreq2 has been replaced by libapreq2-3

The control file has been modified to work with either Apache2.2 or Apache 2.4. To build the package on Debian/Ubuntu:

  sudo apt-get install apache2-prefork-dev apache2-mpm-prefork libapreq2-dev r-base-core r-base-dev devscripts git
  git clone https://github.com/jeffreyhorner/rapache.git
  cd rapache
  debuild -us -uc

If the build succeeded, you can install the package:

  cd ..
  sudo dpkg -i libapache2-mod-r-base*.deb

Alternatively, pre-built packages are available for Ubuntu 12.04 (Precise) up til 13.10 (Saucy) from Launchpad:

  sudo add-apt-repository ppa:opencpu/rapache
  sudo apt-get update
  sudo apt-get install libapache2-mod-r-base

Let us know if there are any questions

Jeroen
